subject: FathomPay TTFT & streaming pilot measurement plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@fathompay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: FathomPay TTFT & streaming pilot measurement plan

Alex — great conversation this morning, thanks for walking through the payment authorization flow. Quick recap and a proposed measurement plan so we all stay aligned before the pilot kicks off.

Summary of performance goals you called out (please correct if I misheard):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target median <= 150 ms, 95th <= 300 ms, 99th < 500 ms for single-request user interactions.
- Sustained concurrency target: 150–200 concurrent inference sessions during peak windows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~250 req/min with short bursts to 600 req/min for batch reprocessing jobs.
- Streaming model preference: you want a streaming UI for partial authorization responses; you said WebSocket would be preferred but SSE is an acceptable fallback.
- Chunk cadence: UX ideally wants first chunk within the TTFT target, then subsequent 100–200 ms cadence for small payloads (10–50 token deltas); you're concerned about too-frequent tiny chunks causing jitter.

Proposed pilot scope (attached): two-week pilot with instrumented traffic, baseline A/B using your current model vs Redwood-optimized serving, and a joint dashboard for TTFT/percentiles, chunk timing distribution, and error/connection drop rates. Pilot deliverables:
- Week 0 (setup): config + security + sample traffic profile ingestion.
- Week 1: synthetic load and smoke tests; measure TTFT under varying concurrency.
- Week 2: run production sampled traffic (shadow) with live telemetry; final SLO report and optimization suggestions.

What we need from you to start:
1) A sample traffic profile (JSON) showing request sizes, typical prompt lengths, and burst patterns.
2) Decision on transport (WebSocket preferred) and any firewall/proxy constraints for persistent connections.
3) Ops contact to provide IP allowlist or VPN details for the private pilot topology.

I've attached a short pilot_scope.xlsx and a small benchmark_script.sh that our infra team will run against a staging endpoint. Ben and Grace are looped for engineering and pilot ops.

Next steps: if this looks right, Ben will send the staging endpoints and a quick runbook by EOD.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@fathompay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, ops@fathompay.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FathomPay TTFT & streaming pilot measurement plan

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful and aligns with what we talked about. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT percentiles: the 95th of 300 ms is acceptable, 99th <500 ms is ideal but we understand tail will need tuning. Can you confirm whether the 99th target refers to user-facing latency (after network) or just server-side processing? We need the user-facing metric for SLAs.

- Transport: WebSocket preferred for our interactive dashboard. Our ops team is behind an outbound proxy that terminates long-lived TLS for WebSocket connections — will Redwood support WebSocket with proxied TLS, or do we need to open a persistent connection from our side?

- Chunk cadence: we prefer fewer, slightly larger chunks rather than frequent 50ms micro-chunks. First chunk should contain the token that signals a successful pre-check (so UI can optimistically enable the confirm button). After that, 150–200 ms cadence is fine.

Looping in ops@fathompay.com to answer the networking question and procurement for PO cadence.

On the other asks: attaching our sample traffic profile.

— Alex
Lead Product Manager, FathomPay
[Attachment: fathompay_sample_traffic.json (application/json)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@fathompay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FathomPay TTFT & streaming pilot measurement plan

Alex — thanks for the sample profile, that helps. A few engineering notes and the pilot runbook we'll use: 

Engineering clarifications:
- Metric mapping: we'll collect both server-side TTFT (time when first token exits model pipeline) and end-to-end RTT from client to first-byte as seen by our edge (where possible). We'll tag metrics so you can see both and we can correlate with your client-side telemetry.
- 99th percentile: we'll report both 99th server-only and 99th end-to-end. For SLA conversation, we'll use end-to-end with an agreed client-side instrumentation practice.
- WebSocket support: Redwood supports WebSocket over TLS through typical proxies. The important detail is that some proxies buffer small writes — if your proxy does that, chunk cadence will appear batched. Can ops confirm whether the proxy does write coalescing. If so, we can recommend an outbound keepalive + Nagle disable on the proxy or fallback to SSE for simpler proxies.
- Chunk sizing: we'll implement a configurable chunking policy on the pilot endpoint so we can test 100ms vs 200ms cadence and 50 vs 150 token chunk thresholds.

Pilot runbook (high level):
1) Setup staging endpoint + TLS certs (day 0–1).
2) Run synthetic suite at 25%, 50%, 100% of target concurrency and gather TTFT/percentile distributions (day 2–4).
3) Shadow live traffic (sampling ~10%) for two business days; collect chunk cadence histograms and connection stability (day 5–7).
4) Run a focused stress test to simulate bursts to 600 req/min and measure degradation modes (day 8–9).
5) Final report, recommended config changes (quantization, batching, routing), and an ops handoff doc (day 10).

Deliverables we'll send you: runbook, Grafana dashboards link, a short SLO definition doc (slo_definition.md), and a short list of corner cases we observed historically with payment flows.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo_definition.md (text/markdown)]

- Billing: pilot covered under evaluation credit; if you want an invoice/PO for proof-of-concept support, procurement can raise PO FP-PO-2026-07 and we'll convert to a committed contract if you decide to go to dedicated capacity.
- Ops ask: please confirm whether the outbound TLS proxy performs write buffering/coalescing. If yes, share proxy vendor/version and we will provide a standard proxy config to avoid chunk coalescing.

Action items assigned:
